name: claims123
description: 123 agents over daedalus/ asking one question: does each docstring and comment claim hold against the code directly beneath it
_size: Exactly 123 units by construction: scan capped at 100 with --limit 100, then 15 + 6 + 2 buckets. Without the cap the scan tier is one unit per chunk of every tracked module (~250) and the run would not be the size that was asked for.
_why_this_target: Three docstring-versus-code defects were found BY HAND in this repository on 2026-07-30, and they are the calibration for this run: providers/base.py promised handoff.suggestions while writing handoff.suggested_files seven lines below; fallback.py said it decides 'when Claude is missing or blocked' while its first branch handles Claude present and succeeding; eval/correctness.py documented a parser that reads a pytest verdict, and it returned not_run for a test pytest had just PASSED. A swarm that finds none of that class found nothing. All three are FIXED at HEAD, so they will not appear -- what should appear is the rest of the same class.
_braces: Every literal brace in `intro` and `task` is doubled. Both strings go through str.format, so a single { is read as a field name -- an earlier draft of this file put a JSON example in `task` and the run died with KeyError('claim') before spending anything.
_no_example_key: There is no `example` key in this schema; only intro, task and fence reach the model. The populated worked example therefore lives INSIDE `task`. It is populated on purpose: the default report template ends its example with an empty list, and 692 of 736 answers in the 2026-07-30 run copied that exact shape.
_lane_note: Advisory only. Model output here is a hypothesis generator, not evidence under section 4 of the master plan, and it promotes nothing. Every finding must carry a named check a human can run.

tiers.name: scan
tiers.intro:
FILE: {module}  (chunk {index} of {total}, starting at line {first_line})

Much of this codebase is machinery that ENFORCES a policy -- guards, gates, contracts, hooks, ledgers, inventories. For that kind of code the gap between what a docstring promises and what the code does is not a documentation defect, it is the failure itself, because the docstring is what every reader downstream believes and acts on.

tiers.name: research
tiers.intro: You hold {inputs} claim rows harvested from separate chunks of one agent kernel. The KEPT rows were dropped before you saw these: what remains is BROKEN and UNCHECKABLE only.

tiers.name: review
tiers.fence: HYPOTHESES, WITH THE REAL SOURCE THEY CITE
tiers.intro: Each hypothesis below arrives with the ACTUAL source of every reference it cited. Where a citation could not be resolved you will see NOT PRESENT IN FILE or a missing excerpt -- that is a refutation on its own, and the strongest kind, because it means the finding was reconstructed from a memory of what a project like this ought to contain rather than read.

tiers.name: plan
tiers.intro: Refuted findings were dropped before you saw these. Everything here survived a reviewer whose whole job was to kill it.
